operators.notes: Tiny table (25 rows), single match → extract one nationkey scalar
Iterate shared supplier hash table, filter by SA nationkey, build lookup map of SA suppliers
Scan shared orders output, set bits for orderkeys with status F. Bitset indexed by o_orderkey (max 60M), ~7.5MB memory. Orders are dense PKs so bitset is ideal.

operators.description: Single sequential pass over lineitem, processing rows in orderkey-group batches. Lineitem is physically sorted by l_orderkey (dense_range index confirms this). For each orderkey group:
per_group_logic: 1. Skip group if orderkey NOT in f_orders_bitset (fast bitset lookup)
2. For qualifying F-order groups, collect per-row: (suppkey, is_late) where is_late = (l_receiptdate > l_commitdate)
3. Identify l1 candidates: rows where suppkey ∈ sa_supplier_map AND is_late = true
4. For each l1 candidate, check EXISTS: group has at least one row with suppkey ≠ l1.suppkey
5. For each l1 candidate passing EXISTS, check NOT EXISTS: no other row in group has (suppkey ≠ l1.suppkey AND is_late = true)
6. For each row passing all checks: increment thread-local aggregation[s_name]++

operators.notes: ~4000 SA supplier names. Merge per-thread maps into single global map.
Only 4000 groups → full sort is fine, no need for heap-based top-K

parallelism.partitioning: lineitem scan partitioned by orderkey ranges across threads; each thread processes contiguous orderkey groups
parallelism.notes: Steps 1-3 are single-threaded (tiny inputs). Step 4 lineitem scan is parallel with thread-local aggregation. Step 5 merge and step 6 sort are single-threaded (small output).

indexes.purpose: Confirms physical sort order by l_orderkey; enables group-boundary detection during sequential scan and morsel partitioning by orderkey range
